name: Model routing with opusplan and fallback chains
what: opusplan uses Opus for planning and Sonnet for execution; --fallback-model or fallbackModel switches when the primary is overloaded.
why_for_gordon: Darby plans on Opus, executes cheap, and survives a 529 storm without a human.
how: claude --model opusplan --fallback-model sonnet; ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL pins the fast model

name: OpenTelemetry metrics and events export
what: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 with OTLP or Prometheus exporters emits cost, tokens, tool decisions, API errors and prompts per session.
why_for_gordon: Darby's Grafana-style health board gets real per-job token and cost series instead of log scraping.
how: export CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=prometheus; or OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp to a local collector

name: Audit log every tool call with a hook
what: A PreToolUse or PostToolUse command hook can append tool_name and inputs to a log file, giving a tamper-evident local audit trail.
why_for_gordon: Every command Darby ran overnight is on disk for the morning postmortem.
how: hooks.PostToolUse matcher "*": jq -c '{t:now,tool:.tool_name,in:.tool_input}' >> ~/claude-audit.jsonl

name: Block dangerous commands deterministically
what: A PreToolUse hook returning permissionDecision deny stops rm -rf or any pattern before it runs, regardless of model judgment.
why_for_gordon: Hard guardrails on Darby's imsg and mail scripts: no sends without safe_send.py.
how: hooks.PreToolUse matcher Bash, if "Bash(rm *)", command block-rm.sh emitting {"hookSpecificOutput":{"permissionDecision":"deny"}}

name: Preprocess verbose output in a hook
what: A PreToolUse hook can rewrite a test command with updatedInput to return only failures, shrinking tokens from thousands to hundreds.
why_for_gordon: Darby's log-check job greps ERROR lines before Claude ever reads the file.
how: hook returns {"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow","updatedInput":{"command":"npm test 2>&1 | grep -A5 FAIL"}}}

name: Security guidance plugin reviews Claude's own code
what: Hook-based plugin pattern-checks each edit, runs a background security diff review each turn, and an agentic review on commits.
why_for_gordon: Site and app code Darby writes gets an independent security pass before it reaches GitHub Pages.
how: /plugin install security-guidance@claude-plugins-official; add .claude/claude-security-guidance.md and security-patterns.yaml

name: /security-review and the Claude Security plugin
what: /security-review does a single pass over branch changes; the Claude Security plugin runs a multi-agent scan and writes SARIF plus patches you apply.
why_for_gordon: Before shipping the GGP directory, run a deep scan and apply each F<n>.patch via its own PR.
how: /security-review; /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official then /claude-security; git apply CLAUDE-SECURITY-<ts>/patches/F1.patch

name: Treat inbound messages as claims, never consent
what: Cross-session messages arrive labeled as from another session, cannot approve prompts, cannot change config, and slash commands in them are inert.
why_for_gordon: The exact model Darby should apply to Astra and iMessage input: notification text is a claim, not a warrant.
how: crossSessionInbound accept|hold|refuse; isolatePeerMachines: true; deny SendMessage and ListAgents to disable

name: Allowlisted API domains can still exfiltrate
what: Cowork incident: an attacker key embedded in workspace files used api.anthropic.com itself to exfiltrate; fix was a proxy accepting only the session token.
why_for_gordon: Darby's allowlist of api.anthropic.com is not enough; strip foreign credentials at the proxy.
how: Run a MITM proxy that accepts only the provisioned token and rejects other Authorization headers

name: Persistent memory is an injection surface
what: CLAUDE.md, auto memory and workspaces reload on every start, so a poisoned note persists; inspect what gets written to memory.
why_for_gordon: Darby's 'memory needs a receipt' rule is exactly the mitigation; audit MEMORY.md diffs in backups.
how: Review memory writes in /memory; keep memory files in git; InstructionsLoaded hook logs which files loaded

name: Privacy switches and retention facts
what: Consumer training opt-out sets 30-day retention; DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC cut background traffic.
why_for_gordon: Chosen-family and student material stays private; Selena reads gbellamy, the audit stays local.
how: claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls; env CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND=1

name: Disable slash commands in a session
what: --disable-slash-commands turns off all skills and commands so untrusted or scripted input cannot expand a /command.
why_for_gordon: Piping student submissions or inbound iMessage text through claude -p cannot trigger a skill by accident.
how: claude -p --disable-slash-commands "..."

name: Graceful shutdown semantics
what: SIGTERM exits 143, kills child Bash processes, runs SessionEnd hooks, and leaves the turn resumable; SIGINT ends the turn cleanly first.
why_for_gordon: launchd stop and restart of Darby workers no longer corrupts state; send SIGINT before SIGTERM.
how: kill -INT <pid>; sleep 2; kill -TERM <pid>; later claude -p --resume <sid>

name: Debug a config with a clean CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
what: --safe-mode disables all customizations; pointing CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at an empty dir bisects whether ~/.claude or the project is the culprit.
why_for_gordon: Fastest way to find which Darby hook or MCP server is hanging the 2-minute Astra watcher.
how: claude --safe-mode; cd /tmp && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/claude-clean claude; claude --debug=mcp; /doctor

name: Bound background waits in print mode
what: claude -p waits up to 10 minutes idle for background subagents; CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS changes or removes the cap.
why_for_gordon: A stuck subagent cannot hold a cron job open forever on the Mini.
how: CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=120000 claude -p "..."

name: Forward subagent transcripts in the stream
what: --forward-subagent-text emits subagent text and thinking with parent_tool_use_id so the full nesting tree can be rebuilt.
why_for_gordon: Post-incident review of a Darby run can see exactly what each Haiku side worker decided.
how: claude -p ... --output-format stream-json --verbose --forward-subagent-text (v2.1.211+)

name: Classify every shell command
what: autoMode.classifyAllShell suspends narrow Bash allow rules in auto mode so the classifier sees every command.
why_for_gordon: A safe-looking allow rule prefix cannot smuggle a destructive argument past review on the Mini.
how: {"autoMode":{"classifyAllShell":true}} (v2.1.193+)

name: Inspect and critique auto mode rules
what: claude auto-mode defaults, config and critique print built-in rules, your effective config, and AI feedback on custom rules.
why_for_gordon: Gordon can read exactly what Darby is allowed to do before trusting an overnight run.
how: claude auto-mode defaults --label 'Git Destructive'; claude auto-mode config; claude auto-mode critique; claude auto-mode reset

name: Review and retry classifier denials
what: /permissions has a Recently denied tab; press r to let the model retry, and a PermissionDenied hook captures the exact tool_input.
why_for_gordon: Darby's denial log becomes a tuning list for autoMode.environment rather than a mystery.
how: /permissions -> Recently denied; hooks: {"PermissionDenied":[{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"jq . >> ~/denials.log"}]}]}

name: Permission rule syntax and the space before star
what: Bash(git diff *) prefix-matches with a space; Bash(git diff*) also matches git diff-index; deny beats ask beats allow.
why_for_gordon: Avoids the classic allowlist bug when Darby's settings pre-approve git and build commands.
how: "permissions":{"allow":["Bash(npm run *)"],"deny":["Bash(git push *)"]}

name: Restricted mode for shared machines
what: --restricted removes command and code tools unless explicitly named and refuses bypassPermissions.
why_for_gordon: A classroom demo or a GGP volunteer laptop can run Claude with no shell access at all.
how: claude --restricted (v2.1.248+)

name: Critical-path removal guard
what: rm -rf targeting / or ~, even inside $(...), is never auto-approved by any allow rule or hook; dontAsk denies it outright.
why_for_gordon: An injected 'clean up' instruction cannot wipe the Mini's home directory.
how: Built in; classifier reviews in auto mode, prompts in Manual, denies in dontAsk

name: Disable bypass permissions org-wide
what: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode set to disable in managed settings removes --dangerously-skip-permissions everywhere.
why_for_gordon: GGP's shared Claude org can guarantee no volunteer runs the nonprofit's repos with all checks off.
how: managed-settings.json: {"permissions":{"disableBypassPermissionsMode":"disable"}}

name: Fail closed when the sandbox is unavailable
what: sandbox.failIfUnavailable makes a missing sandbox a hard error instead of a warning that runs unsandboxed.
why_for_gordon: If bubblewrap breaks on a Linux runner, GGP's automation stops rather than running wide open.
how: {"sandbox":{"enabled":true,"failIfUnavailable":true}}

name: Sandbox denyRead over the home directory
what: Default sandbox read access covers the whole disk; denyRead ~/ with allowRead for projects re-opens only what a job needs.
why_for_gordon: Darby's course-prep job can read the syllabus folder and nothing else in Gordon's home.
how: {"sandbox":{"filesystem":{"denyRead":["~/"],"allowRead":["~/projects"]}}}

name: Reference devcontainer with default-deny firewall
what: The anthropics/claude-code .devcontainer ships init-firewall.sh, persistent volumes and a non-root user so skip-permissions is contained.
why_for_gordon: Students in CTIN 463 can get an identical, walled Claude environment via Codespaces.
how: Copy .devcontainer/ (devcontainer.json, Dockerfile, init-firewall.sh); never mount ~/.ssh; set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to the volume

name: Hardened container flags for agents
what: Run with --cap-drop ALL, --read-only, --network none plus a Unix-socket proxy that injects credentials so the agent never sees keys.
why_for_gordon: Blueprint for a GGP automation box where prompt injection cannot exfiltrate anything.
how: docker run --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --read-only --network none --user 1000:1000 -v proxy.sock ...

name: Credential proxy pattern
what: Route API calls through a proxy outside the agent boundary that injects the key; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or HTTPS_PROXY point Claude at it.
why_for_gordon: Darby's jobs can run without any Anthropic key on disk in the agent's environment.
how: export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 with Envoy credential_injector or LiteLLM adding the header

name: Never mount credential files into agents
what: The secure deployment guide lists .env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.kube/config, *.pem as files to exclude even read-only.
why_for_gordon: A checklist for what Darby's sandbox and any GGP CI image must never expose.
how: Copy only needed sources; use .dockerignore-style filtering; prefer repo-scoped short-lived tokens

name: Login expiry warning for unattended sessions
what: Claude Code warns three days before a /login credential expires; background and Remote Control sessions stall once it lapses.
why_for_gordon: Darby's health check should read /status for the Login row so relays do not die quietly.
how: Renew with /login; /status shows 'Expired' when the saved login is dead (v2.1.210+)

name: Never commit keys; scope Actions permissions
what: Store ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN as GitHub Secrets, grant only needed permissions, and cap --max-turns and timeouts.
why_for_gordon: Baseline hygiene for GGP's repos before any @claude workflow lands.
how: anthropic_api_key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}; claude_args: "--max-turns 5"; timeout-minutes; concurrency groups

name: Scheduled GitHub Actions job with Claude
what: A schedule cron trigger plus a prompt input runs Claude in automation mode; tools must be granted explicitly.
why_for_gordon: A 9am daily report on GGP issues and commits without touching the Mini.
how: on: schedule: cron "0 9 * * *"; claude_args: --allowedTools "mcp__github__list_commits,mcp__github__list_issues"

name: Green run status is not task success
what: Routine run lists show green for infrastructure success only; read the transcript to confirm the task actually happened.
why_for_gordon: Darby's receipts must check outputs, not exit codes, the same lesson as its render-truth toolkit.
how: Open each run session; look for blocked network requests, missing connector tools and task-level failures

name: Local /loop with jitter and seven-day expiry
what: /loop 5m re-runs a prompt while the session stays open; fires send full context, get up to 30 minutes jitter, expire in 7 days.
why_for_gordon: Good for babysitting a Pages deploy, wrong for Darby's daily jobs; use launchd or Desktop tasks instead.
how: /loop 5m check the deploy; CronList/CronDelete to manage; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 to turn off

name: Guardrails for missed or late scheduled runs
what: A missed daily task runs once on wake, possibly hours late, so prompts should check the clock and skip stale work.
why_for_gordon: Darby's morning brief should not fire at 11pm as if it were 7am.
how: Add to prompt: 'If it is after 5pm, skip the review and post a summary of what was missed'

name: Session transcripts and where they live
what: Sessions are JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl, swept after cleanupPeriodDays (30); the format is internal and changes.
why_for_gordon: Darby's nightly backup should snapshot this tree but parse it via /export or -p --resume, not raw.
how: claude -p --resume <sid> --output-format json "summarize what we changed" | jq -r .result

name: Purge a project's local state
what: claude project purge deletes a project's transcripts, tasks, debug logs, file-history and matching history.jsonl lines, with --dry-run.
why_for_gordon: Clean up after a one-off USC grading run so student text does not linger on the Mini.
how: claude project purge ~/work/repo --dry-run; then --yes; --all for everything

name: Checkpoints and /rewind
what: Every prompt snapshots Claude's file edits (100 most recent) so /rewind restores code, conversation or both; Bash edits are not tracked.
why_for_gordon: Cheap undo when a site rebuild goes sideways, but git stays the real safety net.
how: /rewind or Esc Esc; snapshots swept after cleanupPeriodDays

name: Resume from a summary after a long break
what: On Pro or Max, resuming a 100k+ token session after an hour offers to compact first so later turns carry a summary.
why_for_gordon: Gordon's marathon syllabus sessions stop paying full-context prices the next morning.
how: Choose 'Resume from summary' in the dialog; or /compact before the break

name: Share cache across machines for fleets
what: --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections moves per-machine sections into the first user message so identical jobs on different hosts share a cached prefix.
why_for_gordon: If Darby ever runs on both the Mini and a cloud box, the system prompt caches once.
how: claude -p --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections ...

name: Newer tokenizer costs about 30 percent more tokens
what: Claude 4.7 and later use a tokenizer that produces roughly 30 percent more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6 and earlier.
why_for_gordon: Explains why Darby's token counts jumped after the Opus 4.7 upgrade; budget accordingly.
how: Compare token counts per model in /usage or the Usage API before changing models

name: Workspace spend and rate limits for Claude Code
what: Console workspaces get their own spend limits and per-limiter rate caps; the auto-created Claude Code workspace can be capped separately.
why_for_gordon: Cap GGP's Claude Code workspace so a runaway job cannot starve the website's production API keys.
how: Console -> Settings -> Limits -> workspace; set ITPM below org total

name: Claude Code Analytics API per user per day
what: /v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code returns sessions, lines added, commits, PRs, tool accept rates and cost per model per user.
why_for_gordon: Report Claude Corps volunteer impact to the GGP board with numbers, not vibes.
how: GET .../usage_report/claude_code?starting_at=2026-09-12 with an Admin API key; free to call

name: Session, weekly and Opus-specific limits
what: Session limits reset every 5 hours; Max plans add a weekly cap across all models, plus model-specific limits you can dodge with /model.
why_for_gordon: Darby should schedule heavy Opus work early in the week and fall back to Sonnet when the Opus bucket empties.
how: Watch rate_limits.five_hour and seven_day in the status line; /model sonnet when 'You've hit your Opus limit'

name: Cap subagent depth and concurrency
what: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH (default 3) and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS (default 20) bound fan-out cost.
why_for_gordon: Prevents an agent-collaboration experiment with Astra from spawning a token avalanche.
how: env: {"CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH":"2","CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS":"5"}

name: Effort levels to trade tokens for depth
what: --effort low through max sets reasoning depth; medium cuts token use for cost-sensitive work and changing effort mid-session can bust the cache.
why_for_gordon: Darby's routine triage runs at low effort; syllabus design gets high.
how: claude --effort medium; /effort; CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; effortLevel setting

name: Cost center attribution with resource attributes
what: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES tags every metric with department, team or cost_center; cardinality flags control session and account IDs.
why_for_gordon: Split Darby's spend into USC, GGP and personal buckets automatically.
how: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=project=ggp,cost_center=nonprofit; OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID=false to shrink cardinality

name: Distributed tracing beta with TRACEPARENT
what: CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 emits spans per interaction, LLM request, hook and tool, propagating TRACEPARENT into Bash subprocesses.
why_for_gordon: Trace a slow Darby run end to end, including which hook or MCP call ate the time.
how: export CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp; OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 for arguments

name: Audit settings changes with ConfigChange hooks
what: ConfigChange fires when a settings file changes mid-session so you can log or block edits that widen permissions.
why_for_gordon: Detects an injected run trying to rewrite Darby's allow rules or add an MCP server.
how: hooks.ConfigChange command that logs the diff; allowManagedHooksOnly keeps only managed hooks

name: Code Review on PRs and /code-review locally
what: Managed Code Review posts severity-tagged inline findings on PRs; /code-review reviews a diff locally with --fix, --comment, and effort levels.
why_for_gordon: Student capstone PRs and GGP contributor PRs get consistent review; REVIEW.md tunes what counts as Important.
how: /code-review high --fix; @claude review on a PR; gate merges by parsing bughunter-severity from the check run

name: Web fetch in an isolated context
what: WebFetch runs in a separate context window and checks hostnames against Anthropic's safety blocklist so fetched pages cannot inject the main conversation.
why_for_gordon: Darby's research jobs can read arbitrary pages with lower injection risk; pair with WebFetch(domain:) rules.
how: Built in; skipWebFetchPreflight: true disables the check, so keep WebFetch permission rules

name: Restrict models org-wide
what: availableModels and enforceAvailableModels in managed settings limit which models users can pick, including the default.
why_for_gordon: Keep GGP volunteers on Sonnet so shared usage credits are not drained on Opus.
how: managed-settings.json {"availableModels":["sonnet","haiku"],"enforceAvailableModels":true}

name: Slack intake triage with two pasted messages
what: One remember-for-this-channel message gives a request channel a standing role (answer, flag duplicates, route); a Friday rollup sweeps posts that never tagged Claude.
why_for_gordon: An #ask-ggp channel where scholars and partners post questions gets triaged without a person on duty.
how: Paste @Claude remember for this channel: ... then @Claude every Friday at 3pm, post a summary ... including posts that didn't tag you

name: A Slack channel of your own with Claude
what: A channel holding just you and Claude accumulates memory, runs routines, digests channels you don't follow, chases your commitments, and covers time away.
why_for_gordon: Gordon gets a Slack-side Darby for GGP: Monday sweep of promises, Friday digest, pinned out-of-office handoff.
how: Create a channel, /invite @Claude, save remember-for-this-channel instructions, schedule sweeps with an explicit timezone

name: API credentials Claude never sees
what: On Pro and Max, an API key stored on a cloud environment is attached by Anthropic's agent proxy after requests leave the VM.
why_for_gordon: Cloud sessions call a service on Darby's behalf without the key ever entering Claude's context or environment variables.
how: Edit environment > API credentials below Environment variables; not yet available on Team or Enterprise

name: Move a Pro account into a Team org
what: Close your personal account > Bring your data with you moves chats, projects, files, and memory; custom skills and published artifacts stay behind.
why_for_gordon: Directly relevant to the blocked GGP Claude migration: export skills first, cancel App Store billing by hand.
how: Switch to the org account first; irreversible; HIPAA or CMEK orgs cannot receive personal data

name: Claude Campus Program for student leaders
what: Undergrads lead Claude Builder Clubs, master's students host Campus Conversations, PhDs run Science Workshops, each with a $3,600 stipend and API credits.
why_for_gordon: A USC Games student ambassador could feed CTIN 463 and 499 projects with credits, speakers, and demo nights.
how: claude.com/programs/campus; applications ran Sept 1 to Sept 12, 2026 for a Sept 2026 to June 2027 cohort

name: Academy badges with verification links
what: Free Academy courses issue completion badges after lesson quizzes and a final assessment, each with a public verification link that never expires.
why_for_gordon: Gordon can assign Claude 101 as CTIN homework and accept the verification link as proof of completion.
how: Sign in at academy.claude.com with any Claude account; badges appear on the Academy dashboard

name: AI Fluency for Nonprofits track
what: A nine-lesson Academy track with a completion badge that applies the AI Fluency framework to nonprofit work, beside Small Business and Facilitator tracks.
why_for_gordon: A shared onboarding path for GGP staff and board before Team seats roll out.
how: academy.claude.com/courses, choose AI Fluency: For Nonprofits

name: Ask a Slack channel what Claude can reach
what: Sending @Claude what can you access from this channel? lists the channel's connections; the Configure link in any reply footer opens channel settings.
why_for_gordon: Before handing GGP Slack work to Claude, Gordon verifies what the channel can read in one message.
how: Post the question in the channel; click Configure in a reply footer, or send @Claude !configure

name: Pair Slack with a code and a spend cap
what: An Owner sends @Claude connect for a pairing code, enters it at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag, connects services, grants repos, sets a spend limit, launches.
why_for_gordon: A GGP Team plan can turn on Claude Tag in an afternoon with a monthly spend cap from day one.
how: claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag, Owner role required; DMs bill the sender, channels bill the org balance

name: Claude Tag bang commands
what: @Claude !restart replaces a stuck session, !mute and !unmute quiet a thread, !routines lists standing work, !fork #channel prompt continues a thread elsewhere.
why_for_gordon: Recovery and hand-off controls Gordon can teach GGP staff in one line each.
how: The command must directly follow the mention; a thumbs-down reaction on a reply also mutes that thread

name: Respond automatically, per channel
what: Claude Tag reads untagged channel messages and sometimes replies on its own; a per-channel Respond automatically setting makes it mention-only.
why_for_gordon: Keeps Claude quiet in GGP's sensitive channels while letting it jump in on a help channel.
how: Say @Claude only respond in this channel when someone @-mentions you, or flip the toggle on the channel's Configure page

name: Personal connectors inside a shared channel
what: Claude Tag can use your own claude.ai connectors for a task you ask in a channel, with Allow, Allow with review, or Don't allow.
why_for_gordon: Gordon could pull his Google Calendar into a GGP thread without granting the whole channel his calendar.
how: A prompt appears in-thread visible to you; change the saved choice in the Slack Claude app Home tab; limited-availability rollout

name: Custom domain allowlist for cloud sessions
what: An environment's network access can be Custom with your own domain list, wildcards like *.example.com, optionally plus the default package registries.
why_for_gordon: Darby's cloud jobs can reach only the GGP APIs Gordon names and nothing else.
how: claude.ai/code environment dialog > Network access > Custom > Allowed domains; check Also include default list of common package managers

name: Environment cache with a five-minute budget
what: The first session's setup script result is snapshotted and reused for about seven days; scripts must finish in roughly five minutes to cache.
why_for_gordon: Gordon's gamelab toolchain (Node 26, Phaser 4) installs once, then every cloud session starts warm.
how: Parallelize installs with & and wait; move big downloads into a SessionStart hook that runs in the background

name: Line comments in the web diff view
what: Select any line in the diff, type feedback, and comments queue until your next message; then Create PR as full, draft, or GitHub compose.
why_for_gordon: Reviewing a Directory site change from the phone becomes line-level notes instead of paragraphs describing locations.
how: Click the +42 -18 indicator, comment on lines, send your message, then Create PR

name: Excel cell citations and native operations
what: Answers cite cells you click to navigate; Claude also sorts, filters, edits pivot tables, applies conditional formatting, and builds validation dropdowns.
why_for_gordon: GGP scholar rosters and budgets get audited with a clickable citation trail per number.
how: Install Claude for Microsoft 365 from AppSource; ask Walk me through how C42 is calculated

name: Chrome per-site standing permission
what: When Claude hits a restricted site, choose Allow this action, Always allow actions on this site, or Decline; revoke later under Your approved sites.
why_for_gordon: Gordon pre-approves the GGP CMS and Google Docs so Claude stops asking, and revokes in one click later.
how: Claude icon > three-dot menu > Extension settings > Your approved sites; downloads and sensitive entry still prompt

name: Record a browser workflow by doing it
what: In the classic side panel, click record, perform the steps yourself, and Claude learns the workflow; unavailable when the panel runs as Cowork.
why_for_gordon: Gordon demonstrates the IMPACT 200 form once instead of describing every click.
how: Extension panel > record icon, then save the result as a shortcut invoked with /

name: Quick entry: double-tap Option
what: On macOS, double-tapping Option opens Claude over any app; Caps Lock starts and stops dictation on macOS 14 or later.
why_for_gordon: A keyboard-only capture path on the Mac Mini for Darby notes, no window switching.
how: Claude Desktop > Settings > General > Desktop app; Windows not supported

name: Interactive connector cards in chat
what: Asana, Figma, Canva, Slack, Box, Amplitude, Clay, and Hex render live inline cards or fullscreen apps inside the conversation.
why_for_gordon: A GGP Asana board or Canva design gets edited inside Claude instead of a tab hop.
how: On by default when the connector is enabled; Team owners can disable interactive tool calls while keeping text tools

name: Google Docs that sync live in projects
what: Google Docs added to chats and private projects sync from Drive, so Claude reads the current version; Drive picker works in private projects.
why_for_gordon: The CTIN 463 single-source doc stays current in its project without re-uploading each week.
how: Project > Files > Google Drive picker, or paste a Docs URL in chat

name: Usage analytics with Estimated time saved
what: Team Owners see weekly active members, PRs from Code, Cowork sessions, connector activity, and an Estimated time saved figure, plus a CSV spend export.
why_for_gordon: A concrete number Gordon can put in a GGP funder report about AI adoption.
how: Initials menu > Analytics; tabs for Chat, Claude Code, Design, Cowork, Surveys; spend data lags one day

name: Claude LTI inside Canvas courses
what: Admins register a Canvas developer key so Claude launches from Course Navigation and Assignment Edit placements inside the LMS.
why_for_gordon: If USC's Claude for Education org enables it, CTIN students reach Claude from the course shell without a separate login.
how: Canvas Admin > Developer Keys (target https://claude.ai/lti/launch), install the app by Client ID, then Claude org settings > Canvas integration

name: Education org data visibility defaults
what: In Claude for Education orgs, Primary Owner data exports, audit logs, and thumbs feedback stay disabled until the university asks Anthropic support.
why_for_gordon: Gordon can tell students and colleagues exactly what USC administrators can and cannot see in university Claude accounts.
how: Governed by the university agreement; the Primary Owner requests enablement from Anthropic support

name: Admin view of Academy completions
what: Team and Enterprise admins see which courses members enrolled in and their completion status, never quiz scores, attempt counts, or time spent.
why_for_gordon: GGP can track staff AI training for a funder report without surveilling how anyone scored.
how: Members sign in to Academy with the org account; admins view enrollment and completion

name: Claude Tag attachment limits
what: Claude Tag reads images to about 3.75 MB, PDFs to 5 MB, other files to 100 MB, five per message; Slack canvases are unreadable.
why_for_gordon: Saves a silent failure when Gordon drops a syllabus PDF or board deck into a thread.
how: Split large PDFs or paste text; once mentioned, Claude follows the thread without re-tagging

name: Shared cloud environment for a Slack channel
what: On Team plans an Owner creates organization-shared cloud environments with a setup script and points a Claude Tag channel at one for its toolchain.
why_for_gordon: A GGP directory repo channel gets Node and build tools preinstalled for every member's session.
how: Admin settings > Cloud environments; channel sessions use organization-level environments only

name: Quick web setup toggle for Team orgs
what: A Team setting lets members connect GitHub with /web-setup and skips the environment form during onboarding; it is off by default.
why_for_gordon: If GGP moves to Team, this one toggle unblocks Claude Code on the web for staff.
how: Owner turns on Quick web setup at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code after enabling the GitHub connector under Admin settings > Connectors

name: Cloud session sharing with repo verification
what: Sessions toggle Private, Team, or Public visibility; recipients can be required to hold repository access and your display name can be hidden.
why_for_gordon: Gordon can show Astra's or a student's session by link without exposing private repo code to strangers.
how: Session menu > visibility; Settings > Claude Code > Sharing settings for verification and anonymity

name: Per-app Instructions in Office add-ins
what: Each add-in's Settings has an Instructions field applied to every conversation in that app, kept separate across Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
why_for_gordon: Thousand separators in Excel and one-line bullets in PowerPoint, set once for every GGP deck and budget.
how: Add-in sidebar > Settings > Instructions

name: Office add-in chat history stays local
what: Add-in conversations live in browser IndexedDB, never on Anthropic servers, are not synced, and inputs are deleted from the backend within 30 days.
why_for_gordon: A privacy fact Gordon can state to USC or a board when Claude touches a sensitive workbook.
how: Clear history from add-in Settings; note Excel data may flow into Cowork sessions when cross-app mode is on

name: Colored tab group for Claude's tabs
what: Claude opens its tabs in a separate colored tab group and can open, close, and switch among multiple tabs while working.
why_for_gordon: Site QA across GGP pages runs without mixing into Gordon's own open tabs.
how: Built into the Chrome extension; ask Claude to open pages and it groups them

name: Voice mode interrupt, model switch, transcript
what: Start talking to interrupt Claude, pick a preset voice, switch models mid-conversation, and every voice chat saves a text transcript in history.
why_for_gordon: Gordon can plan a CTIN 463 session out loud on a drive and read the transcript later.
how: Sound wave icon; Settings > General for voice; Settings > General > Voice > Language for spoken language

name: Org data export by the Primary Owner
what: Team Primary Owners export conversation and account data from Organization settings > Data and privacy; the emailed link expires after 24 hours.
why_for_gordon: GGP's board can hold a records copy for compliance without a support ticket.
how: Organization settings > Data and privacy > Export Data; deleted messages and projects are excluded

name: Standard versus Premium seat reassignment
what: Owners buy seats; Admins change a member's tier from a dropdown; upgrades prorate immediately, downgrades wait for renewal with no refund.
why_for_gordon: GGP gives Gordon a Premium seat for heavy Claude Code use and keeps board members on Standard.
how: Organization settings > Members > Tier dropdown; Organization and access > Manage under Total seats to buy

name: Dedicated Cowork working folder
what: Anthropic recommends a dedicated folder for Cowork rather than broad access, manual approval for hard-to-undo actions, and pausing unused scheduled tasks.
why_for_gordon: Darby's Mac Mini stays safe if Cowork gets a single GGP working folder and nothing more.
how: Cowork folder access; review past scheduled runs; note Office add-ins may share data with Cowork sessions

name: Claude IT Setup for Nonprofits webinar
what: A five-phase checklist session (identity, data settings, features, launch, migrating existing accounts) with the recording available to registrants on demand.
why_for_gordon: The exact order GGP should follow to stand up a Team plan.
how: anthropic.com/webinars/claude-it-setup-for-nonprofits; July 16, 2026 session, recording within 48 hours

name: Claude certification exams via Pearson VUE
what: Four proctored exams (CCAO-F, CCDV-F, CCAR-F, CCAR-P) issue Credly badges and are open to Claude Partner Network organizations.
why_for_gordon: When a student or GGP partner asks about certification, the honest answer is partner-gated; Academy badges are the public path.
how: pearsonvue.com/us/en/anthropic.html; register through the Anthropic Partner Academy with a partner-domain work email

name: Deploy Office add-ins by manifest XML
what: When an org disables the Office Store, admins upload pivot.claude.ai manifest files as custom add-ins in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.
why_for_gordon: If GGP or USC IT locks AppSource, this is the path to getting Claude into PowerPoint.
how: Admin Center > Settings > Integrated apps > Upload custom apps > Office Add-in; full rollout up to 24 hours

name: Bulk delete chats
what: Chats and tasks > Select > check boxes or Select all > Delete removes chats at once and from backend systems within 30 days.
why_for_gordon: Gordon clears a semester of scratch chats before a data export or an account move.
how: Web sidebar Chats and tasks; on Android use the checklist icon in the chat list

name: Dyslexic Friendly chat font
what: Settings > Appearance offers Default, Match System, or Dyslexic Friendly chat fonts alongside light, dark, and system color modes.
why_for_gordon: An accessibility option Gordon can point CTIN students to on day one.
how: claude.ai/settings/appearance
